articles.title: Escolas e Prefeitura do Rio anunciam 15 escolas no Grupo Especial | G1
articles.standfirst: Gabriel David e o prefeito Eduardo Cavaliere anunciaram o acordo nesta quinta-feira (9). Em 2027, carnaval segue com 12 desfiles, com 2 acessos da série Ouro e uma rebaixada.
articles.summary: Gabriel David e o prefeito Eduardo Cavaliere anunciaram o acordo nesta quinta-feira (9). Em 2027, carnaval segue com 12 desfiles, com 2 acessos da série Ouro e uma rebaixada.
articles.body:
Representantes da Liesa e da Prefeitura do Rio informaram nesta quinta-feira (9) que chegaram a um acordo para que o Grupo Especial do carnaval do Rio tenha 15 escolas. O aumento no número de agremiações de 12 para 15, entretanto, será gradativo e, em 2027, o Grupo Especial segue com o mesmo número de 2026.

A informação foi confirmada pelo presidente da Liesa, Gabriel David, e pelo prefeito do Rio, Eduardo Cavaliere, que falaram com a imprensa.

"A gente chega num acordo de um carnaval de 15 escolas, mas que ele seja feito dentro do regulamento para que aos poucos isso aconteça, progressivamente", disse Cavaliere.

Representantes das escolas se reuniram ao longo da tarde e definiram a fórmula gradual para o aumento. TV Globo apurou que em 2027 o carnaval segue com 12 escolas - duas agremiações subirão da Série Ouro para 2028 e uma vai cair. O sistema será gradual até 2030. O sorteio para definir que dia será cada desfile está previsto para a próxima semana.

"Isso vai demandar uma noite de desfile com 5 escolas. Isso vai demandar mudança de regulamento, e essa decisão compete a Liesa. Uma decisão técnica das escolas e isso eles vão avançar nesse caminho. O papel da prefeitura foi garantir a estrutura financeira para isso, logística, infra-estrutura. Mesmo com a prefeitura garantindo, as escolas precisam de um tempo pra se preparar e planejar", acrescentou.

"As escolas entendem que é viável esse carnaval de 15 escolas, mas a gente entende que é necessário um preparo para isso. A gente vai fazer isso de uma forma gradual. Agora a gente está na discussão exatamente de como isso vai ser feito e vai fazer esse anúncio ainda no dia de hoje", disse Gabriel David. "A gente tem obstáculos estruturais, competitivos, que fazem que essa forma gradual seja a mais prudente".

Abre-alas da Viradouro — Foto: Alexandre Macieira/Riotur

articles.title: Série Ouro: Jacarezinho, São Clemente e Inocentes estão de volta | G1
articles.standfirst: De acordo com a Liga RJ, a recomposição da Série Ouro segue orientação do prefeito do Rio, Eduardo Cavaliere, que indicou publicamente a necessidade de inclusão de mais três escolas no grupo.
articles.summary: De acordo com a Liga RJ, a recomposição da Série Ouro segue orientação do prefeito do Rio, Eduardo Cavaliere, que indicou publicamente a necessidade de inclusão de mais três escola
articles.body:
Comissão de frente da Unidos do Jacarezinho — Foto: Clara Coiote/Riotur

A Liga RJ anunciou o retorno de três escolas para a série Ouro: Unidos do Jacarezinho, São Clemente e Inocentes de Belford Roxo. O anúncio ocorreu no mesmo dia em que a Liesa, que organiza o Grupo Especial, anunciou aumento gradativo no número de suas escolas para 15 agremiações até 2030.

De acordo com a Liga RJ, a recomposição da Série Ouro segue orientação do prefeito do Rio, Eduardo Cavaliere, que indicou publicamente a necessidade de inclusão de mais três escolas no grupo. A Liga afirma que a diretriz foi acatada integralmente, em alinhamento com o compromisso firmado com o poder público e com as próprias agremiações.

Nesse contexto, foi definida a permanência da Unidos do Jacarezinho na Série Ouro. A escola enfrentou dois incêndios durante o ciclo carnavalesco de 2026 — um em seu barracão e outro na quadra —, o que comprometeu sua estrutura e preparação. Segundo a Liga RJ, a decisão foi unânime e considerada um gesto de solidariedade e respeito à comunidade da escola.

Além disso, foram aprovados convites para a entrada de três agremiações: a Inocentes de Belford Roxo, uma das fundadoras da Liga RJ, e a São Clemente, fundadora da Liga Independente das Escolas de Samba do Rio de Janeiro (Lierj). A decisão já foi formalizada junto à Riotur.

A Inocentes de Belford Roxo caiu da Série Ouro para a Série Prata no carnaval de 2026 e São Clemente caiu da Série Ouro em 2025.

A entidade também reforçou a necessidade de avanços por parte da Riotur na resolução de demandas antigas das escolas, especialmente aquelas relacionadas ao uso do espaço público e do Sambódromo, consideradas essenciais para a realização dos desfiles.

Em texto em suas redes sociais, a Liga RJ afirmou que as decisões refletem a vontade coletiva das escolas da Série Ouro e ressaltou o compromisso com a organização do carnaval e a busca pela excelência do espetáculo.

Santuário Nacional de Aparecida — Foto: Lucas Tavares/g1

articles.title: Companhia de teatro abre vagas para curso gratuito em Tatuí | G1
articles.standfirst: Formação terá início em 10 de outubro e segue até 20 de dezembro, aos sábados, com 60 horas de atividades. Não é necessário ter experiência anterior em teatro para participar.
articles.summary: O curso de teatro gratuito em Tatuí da Dupla Companhia oferece 30 vagas para iniciantes, com aulas aos sábados e foco em inclusão social e diversidade.
articles.body:
Curso livre de teatro está com inscrições abertas em Tatuí (SP) — Foto: Lucas Gonzaga

A Dupla Companhia está com inscrições abertas para um Curso Livre de Teatro gratuito, em Tatuí (SP). A formação terá início em 10 de outubro e segue até 20 de dezembro, com 60 horas de atividades e até 30 vagas disponíveis. As inscrições devem ser feitas pelo formulário online .

As aulas serão realizadas presencialmente aos sábados, das 10h às 13h, no Centro de Difusão, Criação e Produção Cultural da companhia, no bairro Doutor Laurindo. Também estão previstas atividades formativas complementares.

Conforme a companhia, não é necessário ter experiência anterior em teatro para participar. O curso é voltado a pessoas interessadas em conhecer ou aprofundar conhecimentos nas artes da cena.

Durante a formação, os participantes terão contato com jogos teatrais, improvisação, interpretação, expressão corporal, voz, memória e dramaturgia. A proposta é investigar as relações entre teatro, memória e identidade, temas presentes no trabalho da companhia.

Ao longo do curso, os alunos também vão participar da criação de um experimento cênico coletivo. O resultado será apresentado gratuitamente à comunidade em duas apresentações no espaço da companhia, ambas com interpretação em Libras.

Segundo a organização, pelo menos 50% das vagas serão destinadas prioritariamente a estudantes da rede pública, moradores de bairros periféricos de Tatuí e pessoas de grupos historicamente minorizados no acesso à cultura, como mulheres, pessoas LGBTQIAPN+ e pessoas com deficiência.

A seleção levará em consideração as informações apresentadas no formulário de inscrição, as cartas de interesse, a disponibilidade para acompanhar as atividades e os critérios de democratização do acesso previstos no projeto.

O projeto do curso foi contemplado pela Política Nacional Aldir Blanc de Fomento à Cultura, por meio da Secretaria de Esporte, Cultura, Turismo e Lazer da Estância Turística de Tatuí, do Ministério da Cultura e do Governo Federal.

articles.title: Seu Jorge e Trio Mocotó ajudam Paulo Ricardo a encarar Marvin Gaye em 'Sangue bom', versão de 'What's going on' | G1
articles.body:
Capa do single 'Sangue bom', de Paulo Ricardo com Seu Jorge — Foto: Arte de Speto

♬ Pedra fundamental da soul music dos anos 1970, o álbum “What’s going on” se tornou marco instantâneo da discografia do cantor e compositor norte-americano Marvin Gaye (2 de abril de 1939 – 1º de abril de 1984), ao ser lançado em maio de 1971, por captar as tensões sociais dos Estados Unidos.

Antes mesmo do álbum, a música-título “What’s going on” fez barulho ao ser apresentada em 10 de janeiro de 1971 em single que antecedeu o LP. Parceria de Gaye com Al Cleveland (1930 – 1996) e Renaldo Obie Benson (1936 – 2005), a música “What’s going on” se tornou um hino contra a Guerra do Vietnã e contra o preconceito racial em ebulição nos EUA. Com uma música, Gaye traduziu todo o estado de ansiedade, fervura e inquietação de um país.

É essa música, repleta de consciência social, que ressurge 55 anos após o lançamento na voz de Paulo Ricardo em versão em português intitulada “Sangue bom” e lançada em single hoje, quarta-feira, 23 de setembro, dia em que o cantor, compositor e músico carioca faz 64 anos.

Avalizada e autorizada pelos herdeiros de Marvin Gaye, a letra em português de Paulo Ricardo aborda a violência contra mulheres e crianças, em tempos de intolerância e radicalismo, e consegue captar um pouco do sentimento dos versos originais de “What’s going on”, sem ser uma tradução.

Embora seja cantor identificado com o universo do pop rock no imaginário nacional por ter sido projetado como vocalista da banda RPM nos anos 1980, sem ter tradição no canto do soul, Paulo Ricardo se cercou de artistas que transitam pelo universo do soul à moda brasileira.

A simples presença de Seu Jorge – cuja voz aveludada carrega toda uma ancestralidade afro-brasileira – contribui para conferir certa legitimidade ao single editado por Paulo Ricardo com capa que expõe obra criada por Speto, artista visual ligado ao grafite e à cultura urbana.

Seu Jorge é grande cantor associado ao samba-rock, gênero formatado pelo Trio Mocotó na virada dos anos 1960 para a década de 1970. Dois ritmistas do Trio Mocotó, João Parahyba (timbales) e Nereu Gargalo (pandeiro), foram arregimentados para a gravação de “Sangue bom”, feita com produção musical do guitarrista Waldo Denuzzo.

Com sopros proeminentes, a sonoridade do single “Sangue bom” é calorosa, mas o groove da gravação poderia ter ficado mais evidenciado na mixagem, já que a intenção foi trazer o standard de Marvin Gaye para o universo rítmico brasileiro.

De toda forma, “Sangue bom” sobressai entre os recentes lançamentos fonográficos de Paulo Ricardo com apuro perceptível já na capa do single. Seu Jorge e os músicos do Trio Mocotó ajudaram o cantor a encarar o hino de Marvin Gaye em gravação bem produzida que consegue escapar por um triz do risco da diluição.

Paulo Ricardo (à esquerda) canta com Seu Jorge uma inédita versão em português da música mais famosa de Marvin Gaye (1939 –1984) — Foto: Bella Pinheiro / Divulgação

articles.title: Malayalam actor Vinu Mohan and Vidya divorce; 13-year marriage comes to an end - Reports
articles.summary: Mollywood actor Vinu Mohan and Vidya were a popular couple among Malayalam audiences. They appeared together in films and stage shows. Their social me.
articles.body: Mollywood actor Vinu Mohan and Vidya were a popular couple among Malayalam audiences. They appeared together in films and stage shows. Their social media presence also made them familiar to their followers.Vinu Mohan and actress Vidya have now reportedly divorced after 13 years of marriage as reported by multiple sites such as Manorama Online, Kerala Kaumudi. The couple got married in 2013 after falling in love through their association with cinema.The couple had regularly shared photographs and videos together on social media. Their posts received considerable attention from fans. However, their absence from each other's social media posts in recent months had led to speculation about their relationship.Vinu Mohan and Vidya's marriageVinu Mohan and Vidya got married in 2013. Their relationship reportedly began through their connection with the film industry. The couple later received the support of their families before getting married.For several years, Vinu Mohan and Vidya remained a familiar pair among Malayalam entertainment audiences. They appeared together at various events and stage shows. Their marriage lasted for 13 years. Reports about their divorce have now emerged, although the exact circumstances surrounding their separation have not been publicly disclosed.Social media activity sparks speculationVinu Mohan had removed photographs featuring Vidya from his Instagram page. Vidya, meanwhile, still has photographs of the couple together on her Instagram account. Her account name also remains Vidya Vinu Mohan.The differences in their social media activity had led to questions among fans. However, neither Vinu Mohan nor Vidya has publicly explained the reasons behind their separation. The two are reportedly planning to move forward with their respective careers. Details about their personal decision have not been made public.Vinu Mohan's acting careerVinu Mohan made his debut as a lead actor with the Malayalam film 'Nivedyam' which turned out to be a superhit. He comes from a prominent family associated with Malayalam cinema.Vinu Mohan is the grandson of veteran actor Kottarakkara Sreedharan Nair. He is also the son of actress Shobha Mohan and the brother of actor Anu Mohan. Actor Saikumar is his maternal uncle. His early filmography includes 'Cycle', 'Chattambinadu' and 'Pulimurugan'.Vidya's film and television journeyVidya began her acting career with the 2007 Tamil film 'Dhandayuthapani'. She later made her Malayalam cinema debut with 'Neelambari' in 2009. The actress went on to appear in several Malayalam films. Her credits include 'Cheriya Kallanum Valiya Policum' and 'Maharaja Talkies'.Vidya has acted in around 15 Malayalam films. She has also appeared in six Tamil films and one Kannada film. Alongside cinema, she has remained active on television.Meanwhile, Vinu Mohan and Vidya got married in 2013 in a star-studded ceremony held in Changanassery, Kerala, followed by a wedding reception in early June 2013.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: The Paradise’: Nani-Srikanth Odela’s ‘A’ certificate action thriller hit the big screens on September 24; here’s what to expect
articles.summary: Nani is gearing up for the one of the most anticipated films of his career as it is reported his biggest film and also the “most tiring” is his long c.
articles.body: Nani is gearing up for the one of the most anticipated films of his career as it is reported his biggest film and also the “most tiring” is his long career of 18 years. The film is set to release in theatres on September 24 after much delays and special screens locked in the evening a prior. There are many expectations from the film as it portrays Nani in a bigger, darker, and rawer character as Jadal reuniting with his ‘Dasara’ director Srikanth Odela.‘The Paradise’ has had a bumpy road to release, earlier it was set for a March 2026 release which later shifted to August. However, after much speculation that it will be further pushed the makers announced a September release. Additionally, the makers have also skipped a conventional trailer release of the film as they were focused on enhancing the final product and other post-production work.No trailer for‘The Paradise’Although they haven’t released the trailer, the other promotional material including the teasers, posters and songs have already created huge buzz and anticipation for the film. Even though the film has received an ‘A’ certificate for its raw and violence content which is considered to cut the family going audience, the early bookings have shown promising numbers.Nani’s transformation as JadalFurther talking about the film, the makers created multiple big sets to capture the slums of the 1980s from Secunderabad where the story is primarily set. Nani has gone under a never seen before transformation for his look as Jadal with the Srikanth Odela at the director’s seat, expectations are that the viewers will get to see a much sharper and stronger film than ‘Dasara’.Nani’s look includes two thick braids, nose piercings, a bindi, and a beefed-up frame that make him nearly unrecognizable.A story about identity and leadershipThe story of the film is set to show a marginalized tribal community who is stripped of its rights and denied citizenship under a deeply entrenched feudal system. Nani's character Jadal is expected to be seen as a leader who unites his people and leads their fight for recognition. The film's guiding line, per its director: "You don't need an identity to be a leader."Mohan Babu and Raghav Juyal as the antagonistsNani is shown as a strong protagonist and strong leads need strong villains. Standing in his way are the feudal lord Shikanja Malik played by Mohan Babu and his ruthless son Vikram Malik played by ‘Kill’ and ‘Bads of Bollywood’ fame Raghav Juyal, locked in a brutal struggle for control over the land called Paradise.Sonali Kulkarni on the mother-son storyInside this conflict, has an emotional core of a mother-son story. Sonali Kulkarni who plays Nani’s mother as Sammakka in the film will be also playing an important role. While speaking with Mid-day, she talked about playing Sammakka and the reason behind the conflict in the film. “Here in The Paradise, I had to understand where we are living, what this fight is all about and what I am thinking as a woman,” she said.The film also features Kayadu Lohar will be seen playing the female lead playing the character Subbalakshmi affectionately called Subbu.Anirudh Ravichander’s music in ‘The Paradise’Musically, with Anirudh Ravichander as the composer, it has been a cultural moment of its own. The intro anthem ‘Aaya Sher’ received huge acclaim. The second single, ‘Yeshanagula,’ brings back ‘Dasara’ co-star Keerthy Suresh while third song ‘Anjaana Anjaani’ is a romantic number featuring the leads.Special show and ticket price detailsA few days ago, a notice issued by Telangana Home Department permitted a special show on September 23 at 6:30 PM, with tickets priced at Rs 500 including GST. Meanwhile, from September 24 to 27, single-screen theatres can charge an additional Rs 48, including GST, while multiplexes and special theatres can charge an additional Rs 95. From September 28 to October 3, the additional charge will be Rs 23 for single screens and Rs 45 for multiplexes and special theatres.‘The Paradise’ advance bookingsAccording to trade analyst Sacnilk, ‘The Paradise’ has sold over Rs. 38.03 crore in advance bookings across six show dates with Hyderabad at Rs. 7.26 crore as of now.‘The Paradise’ will be available in multiple languages including Telugu, Hindi, Tamil, Malayalam, Kannada, English, Bengali and Spanish.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: 'Hanuman Ansh' box office collection Day 48 [LIVE]: Vishal Chaturvedi and Shobhinaw Satyaa's spiritual biopic on Neem Kaorli Baba maintains momentum, crosses Rs 283 crore domestic net milestone
articles.summary: Vishal Chaturvedi’s ‘Hanuman Ansh’ continues to defy expectations as it enters Day 48 of its theatrical run.
articles.body: Vishal Chaturvedi’s ‘Hanuman Ansh’ continues to defy expectations as it enters Day 48 of its theatrical run. The spiritual biopic, led by Shobhinaw Satyaa, has sustained its box-office momentum well beyond its opening weeks and has now crossed the Rs. 280 crore mark in India net collections, aided by a notable jump in overseas numbers that has pushed the worldwide gross to the edge of Rs. 367 crore. The film’s trajectory has been particularly unusual, considering its modest start. After registering limited business in its first two weeks, ‘Hanuman Ansh’ witnessed a sharp upswing from Week 3 and continued to build substantially in Weeks 4, 5 and 6.Having moved past Rs 280 crore in India net, the immediate target for ‘Hanuman Ansh’ is the Rs 285 crore mark. If its extended theatrical run continues to generate steady collections, the film could subsequently aim for Rs 290 crore before approaching the more substantial Rs 300 crore India net milestone. Its unusual week-on-week growth means that the final total could remain dependent on how long the film continues to command screens and audience interest. The film's theatrical run has also received public attention through endorsements from personalities including Kangana Ranaut, Madhur Bhandarkar, Preity Zinta and former Indian cricketer Virender Sehwag, which has added visibility to its spiritual and devotional appeal.'Hanuman Ansh's domestic box office run‘Hanuman Ansh’ began its theatrical journey with Rs. 1.08 crore in Week 1, followed by Rs. 0.40 crore in Week 2. Its fortunes changed considerably in Week 3 when the film collected Rs. 10.40 crore. The momentum strengthened further with Rs. 61 crore in Week 4, Rs. 90.25 crore in Week 5 and Rs. 80.25 crore in Week 6. The film subsequently added Rs. 5 crore on Day 43, Rs. 9.75 crore on Day 44, Rs. 13.75 crore on Day 45, Rs. 4.15 crore on Day 46 and Rs. 4.90 crore on Day 47. Day 48 has so far contributed Rs 0.71 crore from 2,677 shows, taking the India net to Rs. 281.64 crore and India gross to Rs. 332.54 crore.‘Hanuman Ansh’ overseas collection and worldwide totalThe film has also maintained a presence in overseas markets during its extended theatrical run. Its overseas gross stood at Rs 26 crore through Day 45, before adding Rs. 0.50 crore on Day 46. The supplied Day 47 figures indicate another Rs. 1 crore overseas, taking the overseas total to Rs. 34.75 crore. With domestic and international earnings combined, ‘Hanuman Ansh’ has reached a reported worldwide gross of Rs. 366.45 crore.'Hanuman Ansh' Day 48 collection live trackingAs per Sacnilk, 'Hanuman Ansh' is currently running across 6,026 shows on Day 48, having added Rs. 2.82 crore so far in the day.This takes the film's overall India gross to Rs. 335.03 crore and its India net to Rs. 283.75 crore, with the final Day 48 figure expected once all shows for the day have concluded.Day wise collections for 'Hanuman Ansh'Week 1: Rs. 1.08 croreWeek 2: Rs. 0.40 croreWeek 3: Rs. 10.40 croreWeek 4: Rs. 61.00 croreWeek 5: Rs. 90.25 croreWeek 6: Rs. 80.25 croreDay 43: Rs. 5.00 croreDay 44: Rs. 9.75 croreDay 45: Rs. 13.75 croreDay 46: Rs. 4.15 croreDay 47: Rs. 4.90 croreDay 48 [LIVE]: Rs. 2.82 croreTOTAL: Rs. 283.75 croreMore about 'Hanuman Ansh'Written and directed by Vishal Chaturvedi, ‘Hanuman Ansh’ draws inspiration from the life, teachings and spiritual legacy of Neem Karoli Baba. The narrative follows a young boy dealing with a devastating personal loss who embarks on a spiritual journey that introduces him to ideas of faith, compassion, humility and selfless service. Shobhinaw Satyaa headlines the film, with Vihaan Shedge, Chandan K Anand, Purnima Tiwari, Anil Rastogi and Gulshan Pandey among the supporting cast. The film received a U certificate from the CBFC and has an approximate runtime of 2 hours and 30 minutes. It was released theatrically in Hindi on August 7, 2026.DISCLAIMER: The box office numbers and data in this article are compiled from diverse public and industry sources. articles.title: How Ella Langley’s ‘Choosin’ Texas’ became the longest-running No. 1 hit of all time
articles.summary: Ella Langley’s “Choosin’ Texas,” a simmering, midtempo, country-and-then-some heartbreak song released last October, is indisputably 2026’s biggest hit.
articles.body: NEW YORK — Ella Langley’s “Choosin’ Texas,” a simmering, midtempo, country-and-then-some heartbreak song released last October, is indisputably 2026’s biggest hit. “Choosin’ Texas” is also the longest-running No. 1 hit in the U.S., having spent 23 weeks at the top spot on the all-genre Billboard Hot 100, it was announced Tuesday. That means the track has surpassed various records set by Shaboozey’s “A Bar Song (Tipsy),” Lil Nas X’s “Old Town Road,” Whitney Houston’s “I Will Always Love You” and most impressively, Mariah Carey’s “All I Want For Christmas Is You.” Her holiday classic held the previous record, with 22 weeks at No. 1. The song’s laid-back sound, cross-genre appeal and heartache narrative are a few reasons why. But its dominance still comes as a surprise. Here’s how ‘Choosin’ Texas’ became so popular Luminate, the industry data and analytics company, found that “Choosin’ Texas” brought in 911 million on-demand streams in the U.S. and 1.26 billion globally as of mid-August. Considering that Langley started 2023, around the time she made her Grand Ole Opry debut, with under 1 million monthly listeners on Spotify — and now boasts of over 32 million — her rise has been meteoric. Historically, country listenership has centered on radio play. That has changed somewhat as the genre grows in popularity, solidifying around what Luminate’s Jaime Marconette describes as a “younger, streaming-forward listener.” He says it is a “multiyear narrative accelerated” by hits like “Choosin’ Texas.” Claire Heinichen, a senior editor at Spotify, says the song’s growth has been both explosive and consistent. “Choosin’ Texas” “started big,” she says, moving from the platform’s leading country playlist, ‘Hot Country,’ to its larger, generic offerings because it works across audiences. “It made its way into ‘Today’s Top Hits,’ which is our biggest global flagship playlist, but it’s also showing up in ‘Mood’ and ‘Moments’ playlists because it fits so well in ‘driving’ or ‘chill’ or ‘cookout,’” Heinichen says. “It really can work everywhere.” It’s not just country music fans who are connecting with “Choosin’ Texas.” “The song’s success on a playlist like ‘Today’s Top Hits’ is an indication that this is working for audiences who are not seeking out one specific genre,” Heinichen says. “It’s definitely growing in every direction.” The specific sound of ‘Choosin’ Texas’ speaks to its staying power Go straight to Langley’s voice for another explanation for the song’s success. It’s “like syrup,” says Nate Sloan, a musicologist, assistant professor at the University of Southern California and co-host of the podcast “Switched On Pop.” She sings in long phrases that lull the listener into the song’s rhythm, from its opening guitar line to its coda. “It’s almost like a trance,” Sloan says. It also pulls from other genres; a cross-pollination found in much modern country. Langley’s “Choosin’ Texas” features shimmery disco grooves, not unlike Kacey Musgraves. “It’s a little more rock or even kind of soul-inflected,” Sloan says. “Part of the reason songs like ‘Choosin’ Texas’ are able to resonate with such a wide audience is because, musically, they’re bringing in a lot of diverse influences.” Charles L. Hughes, a Rhodes College professor and author of “Country Soul,” says the song sounds like many different eras of country music and, simultaneously, contemporary. To his ears, “Choosin’ Texas” pulls from a late 1970s, early ’80s era of country musicians who pulled R&B and pop into their sound — think Ronnie Milsap, Barbara Mandrell and Charlie Rich — but it isn’t stuck in that period. Those sounds are filtered through a post-Musgraves, post-Miranda Lambert songwriting style, with Langley’s idiosyncratic charms. (Lambert and Langley are two of the song’s four cowriters.) “The best country music has one foot in the past and one foot into the present, if not the future,” Hughes says. “And that’s what she’s doing.” Even for its light, bright musicality, “Choosin’ Texas” is an unusual hit, because it doesn’t possess the features that historically make up a No. 1 smash. It’s super specific — with its detailed descriptions of characters and geography in the lyrics — which is “antithetical to what you usually expect from a big, hit pop song that’s supposed to appeal to everyone,” says Sloan. It’s also “chill,” Sloan says. “It’s not bombastic or anthemic.” “It has no big moments,” says Hughes. But it has both a subtle dance pulse and steel guitar, so “it sounds country, but it doesn’t automatically turn off people who are allergic to certain kinds of country sounds.” There’s a sparkle that transgresses genre lines, but it does so while sounding mellow — the kind of track that inspires repeat listens. The lyrics of ‘Choosin’ Texas’ have a few things going for them “Choosin’ Texas” continues a great tradition of “songs that country women do about what men do in bars,” says Hughes. It’s straightforward: She’s losing her lover to someone else. She’s not going to fight for him — it’s a song of resignation that ends with her drinking alone as he chooses Texas (another woman) over her (and Tennessee). It’s a universal heartbreak theme with potential for cross-generational resonance: It works for both the insecurity of a first breakup and a long-term relationship ending over another woman, or a move. “It’s got these great turns of phrase that give you a little bit of ironic distance as a narrator and as a listener,” says Sloan. “It doesn’t take a crystal ball to see,” Langley acquiesces in the chorus, “A cowboy always finds a way to leave.” The lyrics are also clever, standing out in contemporary country, says Hughes. (Compare it to Luke Bryan’s “Fish Hunt Golf Drink.”) And it’s detailed: Langley’s paramour loves George Strait’s “Amarillo by Morning,” a pantheon Texas track; she’s drinking Tennessee whiskey as a result. “There is the phenomenon of what some critics have called ‘the sad banger’ within the world of pop music,” says Sloan. In country, it’s even more common to take something sad and transform it into something funny or deadpan. “And that’s what she’s really good at, at this song.” ‘Choosin’ Texas’ says a lot about music in 2026 The fact that regular chart-toppers like Taylor Swift, Morgan Wallen and Bad Bunny haven’t released new albums this year could’ve cleared a path for the dominance of “Choosin’ Texas,” but Sloan sees its rise as indicative of something else. “We’re in this environment where you can measure a song’s success in a numerical way,” he says. “But then in terms of its actual cultural impact, that might be more fragmented than you think.” Essentially: “Choosin’ Texas” is on top. But how many people know Langley’s name, the way they knew Houston’s and Carey’s when those hits were released? “It doesn’t feel like a centerpiece of a monoculture, but it is absolutely a key part of like radio culture, streaming playlists, TikTok,” Hughes adds. “But it’s hitting these various audiences in a way that combines to create something huge.” But what does it forecast for Langley? She’s no one-hit wonder: Her award-winning 2024 collaboration with Riley Green, “You Look Like You Love Me” is evidence of that. “It’s always hard to prognosticate with artists when they have an unexpected smash,” says Sloan. “Her ability to write songs with a lot of integrity that both reach back into country tradition and incorporate sounds of the 21st century? That’s a pretty good formula to have a successful and long career in the music world.”

articles.title: Ferran Adrià, chef, da las claves para hacer una tortilla de patatas: "Es una de las grandes cumbres de la gastronomía mundial"
articles.standfirst: El copropietario de 'elBulli', uno de los mejores 50 restaurantes del Mundo, siempre ha sido claro con este tradicional plato
articles.summary: El copropietario de 'elBulli', uno de los mejores 50 restaurantes del Mundo, siempre ha sido claro con este tradicional plato
articles.body: Pocos platos representan la identidad de la cocina española con la fuerza de la tortilla de patatas, y pocos cocineros han reflexionado tanto sobre su técnica como Ferran Adrià. A lo largo de sus distintas intervenciones públicas y publicaciones, el chef catalán ha defendido de manera insistente que la alta cocina no empieza en la centrifugadora ni en los tubos de ensayo, sino en la comprensión profunda de las elaboraciones tradicionales más sencillas. Durante la presentación de su proyecto de cocina cotidiana 'El menú de la familia', Ferran Adrià dejó clara la jerarquía fundamental que debe regir en cualquier cocina: "Primero hay que dominar lo básico: saber hacer un sofrito, limpiar un pescado o hacer una buena tortilla de patatas tradicional. Si no sabes hacer eso con maestría, no puedes pretender hacer cocina creativa ni de vanguardia". Con estas palabras, el cocinero recordaba que el dominio técnico de las bases es la condición indispensable para cualquier innovación posterior. Lejos de la imagen preconcebida que situaba a 'elBulli' como un espacio ajeno a la cocina popular, Ferran Adrià situó a la tortilla clásica en la cima de la gastronomía. En diversos foros del proyecto 'Sapiens' de la 'elBulliFoundation', el chef ha afirma que "para mí, una tortilla de patatas clásica bien hecha —jugosa por dentro, con la patata bien confitada y el huevo apenas cuajado— es una de las grandes cumbres de la gastronomía mundial". Para el cocinero, la clave del éxito reside en la precisión de los tiempos y en el equilibrio térmico al confitar la patata. Esta devoción por la receta clásica no le impidió romper moldes a finales de los años noventa con su famosa "tortilla desconstruida" servida en copa. Como explicó en el documental 'elBulli': Historia de un sueño de TVE, el objetivo de aquella elaboración no era sustituir al plato de toda la vida: "Cuando hicimos en 'elBulli' la tortilla de patatas en copa, usando patatas fritas de bolsa, huevos y cebolla, la gente se llevaba las manos a la cabeza. Pero el concepto no era sustituir a la de la abuela, sino hacer una reflexión: ¿cuáles son los ingredientes de una tortilla? Patata, huevo, aceite y cebolla. Si utilizas una patata frita de bolsa de máxima calidad, rehidratada con el huevo, consigues la esencia del sabor y una textura diferente en tres minutos". Finalmente, respecto a una de las polémicas más célebres de la gastronomía española, Adrià ha ofrecido un análisis puramente técnico. En entrevistas concedidas a medios como El País Semanal con motivo de debates en certámenes como Madrid Fusión, el cocinero valoró el papel de la cebolla señalando que "el debate de si la tortilla debe llevar cebolla o no es una cuestión de gusto personal, pero desde el punto de vista culinario, la cebolla aporta un dulzor y una humedad que ayudan a que el resultado final sea mucho más jugoso". De este modo, el chef demuestra que cada ingrediente debe responder a una función sensorial precisa en el plato.

articles.title: Vivek Oberoi backs Salman Khan’s stand against trolls after he slammed trollers body-shaming him, Katrina Kaif: ‘There are a lot of positive things to do in life, negative mein kya pade ho’
articles.summary: Vivek Oberoi has spoken in support of Salman Khan’s recent comments on online trolling. Salman had called out social media users for body-shaming and .
articles.body: Vivek Oberoi has spoken in support of Salman Khan’s recent comments on online trolling. Salman had called out social media users for body-shaming and age-shaming celebrities, questioning why people resort to abusing actors simply because they do not approve of their work. His comments received support from several celebrities, including Varun Dhawan, Neha Dhupia and filmmaker Rohit Shetty. Vivek has now also agreed with Salman’s stance, saying there is no reason to engage in negativity.Vivek was recently spotted spending time with children battling cancer at an event organised by the Cancer Patients Aid Association (CPAA). During a conversation with Bollywood Chronicle, he was asked about Salman speaking against trolls on 'Bigg Boss 20'. Vivek said, "Kuch nahi yaar, mujhe lagta hai trolling wagera karna bhi nahi chahiye. Trolling is a very negative thing, and there are a lot of positive things to do in life kya negative mein padhe ho (Nothing, yaar. I feel people shouldn’t troll others either. Trolling is a very negative thing, and there are so many positive things to do in life. Why get caught up in negativity?)."Salman had addressed the issue of online trolling during the latest Weekend Ka Vaar episode of 'Bigg Boss 20'. Talking about the scrutiny faced by celebrities over their appearance, the actor revealed that he has also been targeted online and has been called "budha", while social media users have also mocked his new bald look.The superstar also came to Katrina Kaif's defence after she faced criticism over her post-pregnancy appearance. Referring to the trolling directed at the actress, Salman said, "Everyone puts on weight after getting pregnant. When she returns to films, she will get back in shape. She wants to spend time with her family."Salman also addressed the comments aimed at his own physique. In response to those who had body-shamed him, he removed his T-shirt and showed off his toned physique. He explained that his bald look was for an upcoming film and also spoke about the recent death of one of his close friends. Calling out those who make money by putting others down, Salman described online trolls as "parasites".Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Reunion with Srikanth Odela, Nani’s new avatar, Anirudh’s music: 5 reasons to watch ‘The Paradise’
articles.summary: Natural Star Nani is returning to the big screens with the upcoming action thriller ‘The Paradise’ directed by Srikanth Odela. The film has been in pr.
articles.body: Natural Star Nani is returning to the big screens with the upcoming action thriller ‘The Paradise’ directed by Srikanth Odela. The film has been in production since June 2025 and after a couple of delays is finally hitting the big screens on September 24 with some special early shows scheduled in the evening on September 23. Let’s take a look at some of the reasons to watch the film.Reunion of Nani and Srikanth Odela after ‘Dasara’‘The Paradise’ marks the second project between Nani and Srikanth Odela after their 2023 hit ‘Dasara’. The film received huge critical acclaim which captured the rustic authenticity of a coal mine. Given this was Odela's first film, he received appreciation for its polished and confident staging. Now, with ‘The Paradise’ expectations are high for the pair repeating that magic. Recently, Nani shared that he could see Srikanth Odela’s evolution as a filmmaker while speaking with Variety India. He shared that for ‘The Paradise’ Srikanth was in full control of the set unlike ‘Dasara’.“As far as ‘Dasara’ goes, Srikanth comes from this small town called Godavarikhani in Telangana and his dad worked in a coal mine there. He understood that world well and was able to make a film like ‘Dasara.’ But when it came to “The Paradise,” a lot of research was required. When Srikanth was directing ‘Dasara,’ he never imagined he’d do something like ‘The Paradise.’ But the way he has researched and evolved to make a film like this is admirable,” Nani said.Nani’s new avatar in ‘The Paradise’In the film, Nani will be seen playing the character Jadal who seems to be playing a leader of the marginalized community who are fighting for justice and against the oppression. For the film he will be seen donning a brand new look making one of the most talked-about elements of the film. Nani has long hair where he keeps two thick braids while he also wears nose piercings and a bindi, giving him a tribal, rugged aesthetic.Nani has also muscled up his physique as his looks from the films shows a noticeable build. Interestingly, Nani in his 18 years career, called ‘The Paradise’ his most physically demanding look yet. While interacting with the media during the event, the ‘HIT: The Third Case’ actor said, “The Paradise is the most tiring film of my career, both physically and mentally. If there has been a film for which I have worked very hard in these 18 years of my film career, it is 'The Paradise'.”Story of rebellion‘The Paradise’ is primarily set around the 1980's of Secunderabad and in and around a slum settlement. From the promos released one can establish that it is about a marginalized tribal community who is long denied basic rights, citizenship and face systemic oppression. Nani is described to be someone with no conventional standing, who rises from within this community to unite them and fight back.Earlier, Nani himself described the film as "India's Mad Max". It is set to show him in an unhinged avatar, some ruthlessly killings as the film has received an ‘A’ rated certificate from the censor board.Cast of ‘The Paradise’The Srikanth Odela directorial has a star studded cast as it features Nani as Jadal and also includes ‘Dragon’ fame Kayadu Lohar as the female lead. Nani will be seen clashing with the feudal lords who are holding power over the land called "Paradise". It features Tollywood veteran Mohan Babu as Shikanja Malik and Bollywood actor Raghav Juyal as his son Vikram Malik, a ruthless enforcer.The film also has Sonali Kulkarni and Sampoornesh Babu in supporting roles.Anirudh Ravichander’s soundtrackStar musician Anirudh Ravichander is composing songs for ‘The Paradise’. His first single ‘Aaya Sher’ was released as a birthday special for Nani. The song includes tribal percussion and gritty electronic layers, a touch of Anirudh. Folk singers Addula Jangireddy and Akunoori Deviah lend fierce, earthy vocals alongside Anirudh which received huge appreciation from the listeners.Another song, ‘Yeshanagula’ is a special one in the film as it brings back Keerthy Suresh who worked with Nani and Srikanth in Dasara for a special cameo.Recently the makers also dropped the third single, ‘Anjaana Anjaani’ which is a romance number features Nani and Kayadu Lohar.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Presley Gerber’s final hours at rehab in focus amid cause of death questions
articles.summary: Presley Gerber's final hours draws questions. Police are investigating the 27-year-old model's death as a suspected overdose.
articles.body: Presley Gerber died Sunday, Sept. 20 – one day after entering the Resolutions Living rehabilitation facility in Santa Monica, Calif. He was 27. Based off Wilshire Boulevard in an affluent Southern California community, the center is described as a co-ed home which "provides the structure" for residents on their journey to recovery from mental health, addiction, and co-occurring disorders through intensive outpatient programs of their choosing. While it remained unclear why Cindy Crawford's son entered the center or what treatment he was receiving, wrongful death and personal injury attorney John J. Perlstein warned against jumping to conclusions of liability as the investigation continued into Gerber's death. PRESLEY GERBER'S DEATH BEING INVESTIGATED AS 'A SUSPECTED OVERDOSE': POLICE "I just don't assume what the cause of death is or that the facility failed them or the family ... don't think the family wasn't doing everything they had to do," Perlstein told Fox News Digital. "It seems like, you know, in these situations the families do so much for the sick person, the person who was addicted." He added, "By all accounts, they were a very loving, good family, and it's just real sad circumstance. It certainly caught a lot of people's attention. I'll tell you that much." Gerber, the only son of supermodel Cindy Crawford and businessman Rande Gerber, died while staying at the rehabilitation facility, according to records from the Los Angeles County Medical Examiner. KID ROCK CALLS PRESLEY GERBER’S DEATH A ‘TRAGEDY’ AS EX-GIRLFRIEND SAYS HE ‘DESERVED MORE TIME’ The treatment center's website says it draws "on our years of experience in addiction and mental health support," with "experienced staff has supported people with a wide variety of needs, from substance abuse and mental health, to trauma and eating disorders." Gerber reportedly checked into the facility on Saturday night and died Sunday morning. Representatives for Resolutions Living did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment. Nicholas Kardaris, Ph.D., CEO and chief clinical officer of the New York Center for Living in Manhattan and a clinical professor at Stony Brook Medicine’s School of Social Welfare, cautioned against drawing conclusions from the fact that he died at a rehabilitation facility. CINDY CRAWFORD’S SON PRESLEY GERBER SAID HE WAS ‘TERRIFIED’ IN RAW ADDICTION POST MONTHS BEFORE DEATH AT 27 As Gerber’s official cause of death has not yet been released, Kardaris — who has not treated Presley Gerber and is not connected to the case — noted that possible explanations could include an acute medical or cardiac event, an undiagnosed condition or a medication-related complication. People in residential treatment facilities may have complex medical histories, and some conditions may not be immediately apparent when someone enters a program. "Younger people can sometimes die suddenly, and we don’t know whether they had an underlying medical issue," Kardaris said. "It’s not impossible to have a medication-related event, particularly if someone has an underlying heart disorder," he continued. "Certain medications can trigger a cardiac episode." LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS He added, "People are in rehab because they’re struggling with addiction. It doesn’t mean they’re cured of their addiction." Another potential risk during rehab is withdrawal itself, which can range from uncomfortable to life-threatening depending on the substance involved and the person’s level of physical dependence, according to Kardaris. PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE "People can die from withdrawal, but the substances that are most dangerous to withdraw [from] without proper medical supervision are benzodiazepines, such as Valium or Xanax, and alcohol," he said. The deputy medical examiner (DME) told Fox News Digital that "the investigation is still ongoing and there is limited information available," and his cause of death has not yet been released. The DME is in "the early stages of investigating the death of 27-year-old model Presley Gerber and limited information is currently available," according to a statement from the department. GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE "A deputy medical examiner performed an examination today and the cause and manner of death have been deferred, which means additional testing and/or studies were requested in order to make a determination." They added, "Due to the ongoing death investigation, the DME cannot disclose what testing and/or studies were requested. Deferred cases can take a few months before a cause of death is determined." Santa Monica Police Department officials are investigating the death as "a suspected overdose," according to a release from the department. Officers responded to a report of a possible overdose at approximately 9:35 a.m., Sunday, Sept. 20. Upon arrival, officers located an adult male who was deceased. At this time, there is no indication of foul play, and Gerber's case remains open. The facility has not been accused of wrongdoing. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP A representative for the family told Fox News Digital, "The family is asking for privacy during this very difficult and painful time." Fox News Digital's Melissa Rudy contributed to this report.

articles.title: Samay Raina’s 'India’s Got Latent 2' faces fresh controversy as complaint targets Mukesh Chhabra and OTT platform over alleged inappropriate language
articles.summary: Samay Raina’s 'India’s Got Latent 2' has come under fresh scrutiny after a complaint was filed against casting director Mukesh Chhabra and Netflix Ind.
articles.body: Samay Raina’s 'India’s Got Latent 2' has come under fresh scrutiny after a complaint was filed against casting director Mukesh Chhabra and Netflix India over allegedly inappropriate language used during a recent episode of the comedy show.The complaint was filed by Anurag Shrivastav, who has raised concerns over remarks he allegedly heard while watching the episode featuring actor Nawazuddin Siddiqui, actor and YouTuber Bhuvan Bam, Mukesh Chhabra, stand-up comedian Kaustubh Agarwal and host Samay Raina. The episode premiered on September 18 on Netflix and YouTube.What the complaint against Mukesh Chhabra allegesAccording to the IANS report, Shrivastav said he was watching Netflix on his laptop from a Mumbai hotel room on the evening of September 22, 2026, when he came across the 'India’s Got Latent' episode.The complaint alleges that Chhabra was heard making the remark, “Mere Aaram Nagar mein aao, gaand marao.”The complainant described the alleged language as “highly inappropriate, objectionable, and sexually suggestive” and sought verification of the statement before any conclusions are drawn.The complaint itself reportedly acknowledges that “the authenticity of this statement, the identification of the voice/person, the complete context, and the exact timestamp need to be verified from the original and unedited recording.”Complainant questions Netflix India’s roleShrivastav has also questioned Netflix’s role in approving and streaming the content. According to the complaint, if the alleged remark is authenticated, it could raise concerns around viewer dignity and child cyber safety.The complaint has sought an inquiry into how the content was approved for streaming and has also called for an examination of the role of Monika Shergill, Netflix India’s content chief. These remain allegations and requests made in the complaint; there is no indication in the cited report that the claims have been established.'India’s Got Latent 2' has faced fresh controversyThe complaint comes days after the latest episode of 'India’s Got Latent 2' generated discussion online over jokes involving Mukesh Chhabra. The episode also saw Samay Raina make remarks about Chhabra’s girlfriend, while an unverified social media claim alleged that the shoot was briefly halted. Raina later responded to that claim on Instagram with a humorous post, without confirming the reported incident.The episode featured Chhabra alongside Nawazuddin Siddiqui, Bhuvan Bam and Kaustubh Agarwal. Raina also roasted Nawazuddin over his appearance in Thamma during the episode.The show was previously at the centre of a major controversyThis is not the first major controversy associated with 'India’s Got Latent'. In February 2025, comedian and podcaster Ranveer Allahbadia faced widespread criticism over remarks concerning parents and sex during an episode of the show's first season. The controversy subsequently led to legal proceedings and significant public scrutiny of the programme.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Netflix turns Willy Wonka’s chocolate factory into a real-life ‘social experiment’
articles.body: Lickable wallpaper. An edible garden replete with gummy foliage. A chocolate river made of 25,000 gallons of chocolate goop. Nods to the “Willy Wonka & the Chocolate Factory” films appear everywhere in Netflix’s new reality competition show “Wonka’s The Golden Ticket.” But the show, which debuted on the streamer Wednesday, also embraces the darker elements of Roald Dahl’s 1964 children’s book and subsequent films. Unlike the original story, which ultimately rewards protagonist Charlie for his humility and lack of greed after a tour of Wonka’s whimsical chocolate factory, Netflix’s series incentivizes contestants to scheme and strategize to win a $3 million prize. “This is the modern-day take on the movie, so we weren’t really ever trying to be the morality police. We never ever wanted to set out to be the producers that dictated who behaved well and who behaved poorly,” said showrunner Emer Harkin. “Because let’s be real, we’re all human. We all make mistakes. We all misbehave. We seek redemption. We all have our inflected storylines, and so that was important for us.” Yet when the trailer dropped earlier this year, fans of the pop culture classic appeared less preoccupied with the reality twist on the story than with another creative choice: the use of generative AI to replicate the late Gene Wilder’s voice from the original 1971 film. “A whole new generation of real-life Golden Ticket holders will compete for a life-changing prize or say a most unfortunate goodbye,” the AI-generated voice of Wilder says in the series. “Marvel at the magic you remember and delight in my newest wonders beyond imagination. The most extraordinary competition on Earth is about to begin.” The decision is one that Harkin and co-showrunner Alison Holloway stand behind, saying the use of Wilder’s likeness meant to honor him, not diminish his legacy. It was done with explicit approval, and encouragement, from his estate and wife. “The more we developed the series, the more we kept thinking: What would Wonka do at this point? What would Wonka say? i.e., What would Gene Wilder say?” Holloway said. “So it became clear to us that Gene Wilder was perhaps the only voice that could do this.” No in-person hosts appear in the show, but the disembodied AI-generated replica of Wilder’s voice floats in every so often to announce new challenges and contestant terminations. The emerging use of generative AI in Hollywood has stirred pushback from film industry workers, who say they’re worried about loss of labor in an already dismal market for entertainment jobs. When the “Wonka” reality show trailer was released, some fans online suggested that Wilder wouldn’t have signed off on the project if he were alive today, pointing to how he criticized the 2005 “Wonka” remake. Holloway said she understands and shares people’s concerns over AI use. But receiving support from Wilder’s widow, Karen Boyer, made her feel at peace with the decision to proceed with the idea. “I think we have to believe that the people who loved him the most want this to happen,” Holloway said. “And of course, it’s out of total respect for his legacy that we’ve gone to such lengths to get it as best as we can.” In order for the show to capture the cadence, the tone and the “whimsy” of Wilder’s voice, the team behind the show sifted through hours of Wilder’s audiobooks, which Boyer provided to them. Netflix partnered with the AI voice generation company ElevenLabs, which has been making inroads in Hollywood in recent years collaborating with both studios and celebrities. To bring the fictional world to life, Netflix employed a team of working magicians to make the “magic” feel real to the contestants. The competitors, who earned their entry onto the show by finding a golden ticket hidden within a Wonka-themed chocolate bar, arrive at the giant chocolate factory to face off in a phantasmagoria of dramatic candy-colored challenges. In the first challenge of the show, some contestants disappeared in a puff of fog while sitting right beside their partners — extracting reactions that the showrunners said “had to be absolutely authentic.” “We watched that movie over and over and over again, and it gave us the template for the 2026 social experiment,” Holloway said. “We hope we’ve captured all the nostalgia … the magic that was always there, the unpredictability that was always there, the sort of darkness that was always there.”

articles.title: 'Lioness' star weighs in on what drove Taylor Sheridan's unexpected decision for her character
articles.summary: Elizaveta Neretin reacts to Taylor Sheridan's outcome for her "Lioness" character Oleksandra Balakin in the season 3 finale.
articles.body: WARNING: Spoilers below. "Lioness" star Elizaveta Neretin reacted to Taylor Sheridan's bombshell season 3 finale, which saw her character, Oleksandra Balakin, killed off. Speaking to Fox News Digital, Neretin — who played the Ukrainian double agent — said she expected Oleksandra's fate. The character had been captured by American forces and recruited to help rescue Joe (Zoe Saldaña) after she was kidnapped. In the episode, which aired Sunday night, Oleksandra was killed. 'LIONESS' SEASON 3 FINALE REVEALS WHO ORCHESTRATED JOE'S KIDNAPPING ALL ALONG "I thought it was going to happen. So when he called, and he told me, I was like, 'Yeah, I get it.' I'm sad for Oleksandra and what Oleksandra represents, but I understand the choice. It does serve this. It serves to show how the whole system is. Like American or not American, the whole system and the people that work in the system. It's all sharks, you know, so it just demonstrates how people are," she told Fox News Digital. Neretin said she would have preferred a different outcome for Oleksandra but understood why Sheridan made the decision. "I would love a different ending for her, but like I said, I understand why it had to happen." "I would love a different ending for her, but like I said, I understand why it had to happen. But, of course, I would have a good ending for her. I just wonder if being a triple agent, I think your days are numbered. I don't think you can pull that off and live to an old age unless you give up on family you have, which I don't think she would." But the way she fights for her country, I think she cares way too much, way more about that outcome than her life. I think that she made that decision a long time ago," Neretin said. The actress said she never asked Sheridan whether he had considered an alternative ending for Oleksandra. Instead, she trusted his creative judgment and did not try to challenge him while working on the series. "No, I didn't challenge him. I just remember he shortened Oleksandra's name a certain way, and I just suggested, I was like, 'By the way, the short version of Oleksandra in Ukrainian is Alessa.' And he was like, 'Yeah, that works,'" she began. "I didn't challenge him, it was very interesting, like he runs the show, you know what I mean? He's the boss." Nicole Kidman, who plays Kaitlyn in "Lioness," was also asked whether her character felt remorse over Oleksandra's death during an interview with Entertainment Weekly. You're like, ‘Oh my God.’ And that's all we talk about on set the next day, everybody's like, 'Oh my gosh, did you see this?' Yeah, people have bets going what's gonna happen," she said. articles.title: Biswajit Chatterjee recalls giving 'Rocky' title to Sanjay Dutt's debut project, bonds with Sunil Dutt family
articles.summary: Veteran actor Biswajit Chatterjee, who has worked with some of Hindi cinema's biggest stars including Dilip Kumar, Pran, Raaj Kumar, recalled a special
articles.body: Veteran actor Biswajit Chatterjee, who has worked with some of Hindi cinema's biggest stars including Dilip Kumar, Pran, Raaj Kumar, recalled a special chapter from his decades-long journey in the film industry about giving the title 'Rocky' to Sunil Dutt for his son Sanjay Dutt's debut film.In a conversation with ANI, Biswajit revealed that he originally owned the title 'Rocky' for a film he planned to make as a producer-director with Amitabh Bachchan and Rekha. However, the project was eventually shelved, following which Sunil Dutt approached him while launching Sanjay Dutt in Bollywood and requested the title for his son's debut film.The veteran actor recalled that his close relationship with the Dutt family led him to hand over the title without any hesitation."Sunil Dutt said, 'Apne bete ke liye film bana raha hu..yeh title Sanju baba ko bahut suit karega' (I am making a film for my son, Biswajit. This title suits Sanju Babu a lot}. Our relationship with him, Sunil Dutt, Nargis Bhabhi, you know, like a family relationship. I said, take it now," he recalled.Biswajit said that he refused to accept any payment for the title and gave it to Sunil Dutt because of their personal bond."He said, how much money will you take for it? I said, what are you saying...? Next day, I gave it to him. Rocky. I gave the title of the first film..," he said.The actor also remembered the emotional moment linked to the film's release, saying Sanjay Dutt's mother Nargis Dutt could not witness the release of Rocky as she passed away due to cancer.'Rocky' is a 1981 romantic action film directed by Sunil Dutt. This film marks the debut of Sanjay Dutt and also stars Tina Munim, Reena Roy, Amjad Khan, Raakhee, Ranjeet, Shakti Kapoor and Aruna Irin pivotal roles.Biswajit, who became one of the popular romantic heroes of the 1960s with films like 'Bees Saal Baad', 'Kohraa', 'Mere Sanam' and 'Kismat', continues to remain connected with cinema and still enjoys watching films in theatres.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: I need to See Everything now.
articles.summary:
The official trailer for Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim’s Elizabeth Holmes documentary, You Can See Everything has dropped. The movie — which seems to involve Fielder living in Holmes’ home with her born-rich husband and small baby before she heads to prison for the criminal fraud that was Theranos — comes out October 16th.

articles.body:
Elizabeth Holmes sentenced to 11 years in prison for her Theranos fraud

The official trailer for Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim’s Elizabeth Holmes documentary, You Can See Everything has dropped. The movie — which seems to involve Fielder living in Holmes’ home with her born-rich husband and small baby before she heads to prison for the criminal fraud that was Theranos — comes out October 16th.
